parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes Tier-1 universal exposure: birth-sex facilities in airports and other public buildings, enforced by up to $1,000 penalties and private bounty suits, plus national passport sex restrictions and entry-refusal/fraud risk on document discrepancy. No execution or routine imprisonment is credible, but detention and custody have documented severe abuse. National hate-crime and state anti-discrimination protections are partial, state hate-crime law excludes gender identity, and litigation has not stayed the operative restrictions. A visitor has no effective remedy against the facility or entry regime.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports limited to M/F by sex at birth; X not issued since Feb 2025. Entry cable directs refusal on document discrepancy/reasonable doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid to expiration; passport policy is under legal challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: Discrepancy at entry can escalate from refusal of admission to a permanent, lifetime fraud finding, with limited waivers.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports for trans men include forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. From 2026 national corrections adopt birth-sex model including hormone removal, hair cutting and psychiatric substitution; a bathroom arrestee in another state spent 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility or document arrest can lead to birth-sex custody placement and documented abuse, multiplying the initial $1,000/bounty exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law, effective 26 Feb 2026, confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in publicly owned buildings including schools, universities, airports and offices; civil/criminal penalties to $1,000 and bounty suits of at least $1,000 by any private person.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law since 2020 bans gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations, but no documented facility-access exemption or operative pre-emption is shown.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private bounty enforcement does not depend on prosecutors, so a visitor in an airport or government building can be sued even without state action; national facility bans apply in parallel.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in the division and 27 states nationally; proposed federal rules would bar public reimbursement under 18. Custody hormone removal is documented.
care_services.protection: A May 2026 state district judge granted a temporary injunction in a parental lawsuit; scope and continuation are not documented.
care_services.interaction: Routine adult care is not documented as banned, but emergency or custodial discovery can trigger birth-sex ward and hormone interruption.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive order defines sex as birth binary and bars gender-identity facilities; counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; DOJ reward memorandum uses radical gender ideology framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several executive orders have been blocked or enjoined; the 2020 national employment-discrimination ruling remains law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases police and private-enforcer discretion in facility and document encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors are barred from female school sports in the division, confined to birth-sex school facilities, and subject to the care ban. A federal order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition, including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: May 2026 temporary injunction may limit care-ban enforcement; scope not documented. No documented visitor-specific exemption.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces the same birth-sex facility and school rules as a resident; a parent/guardian faces bounty, criminal and child-care-related scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of trans-specific street violence in the division dossier; 66% polled support birth-sex government documents. Bounty system invites private confrontation in facilities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity since 2009; state anti-discrimination law covers employment, housing and public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State hate-crime enhancement excludes gender identity, weakening local recourse, though national law remains available.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions to take effect; state appellate court reversed a restraining order and the highest state court allowed licence invalidation to continue.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties lawsuits are pending on passports and on the 2026 facility/ID law; several other orders are enjoined. Legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation does not suspend the operative birth-sex facility, bounty or entry rules, so remedies are uncertain at time of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine police stops, fines and weak judicial deference without frequent imprisonment. This case is similar or slightly higher because penalties are mainly monetary/bounty and custody abuse is reported nationally rather than routine for visitors.

Lower: 0.55-C has ward placement by document marker with delays and advocacy remedies, but no criminal/bounty facility offence. Here birth-sex facilities are criminalised/civilly penalised in airports and private persons can sue, a Tier-1 universal exposure.

Higher: 0.25-C features birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults and slow remedies as the central visitor risk. Here such custody harm is documented in national immigration/corrections systems but requires arrest/detention first, and execution is not credible, keeping the score above 0.25.

Materially lower: 0.75-C has respectful entry, brief detention only and a tribunal with compensation. Here entry can be refused with permanent fraud risk, facilities are birth-sex by law, and a private bounty regime operates in public buildings.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: a home passport is checked against a birth-binary national regime, entry discrepancy can become refusal or permanent ineligibility, and inside the division birth-sex facilities in airports and public buildings are enforced by fines and private bounty suits. State anti-discrimination and national hate-crime law do not cancel those operative rules, state hate-crime law excludes gender identity, and courts have allowed key restrictions to proceed while challenges remain pending. If detained, documented national custody practices add severe harm. No execution or routine imprisonment is shown, so the score sits in the high-risk band rather than the severe-risk band.
